title: Morphological traits of the eyes of Lepidoptera indicate selection for binocular vision in both diurnal butterflies and nocturnal moths
why: Calephelis and Prionoxystus, acuity_cpd and interommatidial_deg: eye morphology (detectability, resolution, stereopsis) of 2,730 specimens of 224 butterfly and moth species sampled across a tribal-level phylogeny; the harvest abstract does not name genera, so the species table in the full text or its data may include a metalmark (Riodinidae) or a carpenterworm moth (Cossidae). why: Lyrurus, eye_movement and spectral_range_nm: main holds four black grouse rows from this paper (field 353 degrees, binocular overlap, acuity 9.81 cycles per degree estimated from axial length, SWS1 peak 393 nm), read in part through a summariser. It came back first for the web searches "black grouse eye movement" and "black grouse spectral sensitivity". Authors, title and DOI from main's rows (birds, sweep-17).
